prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

Summary of key proposals and commitments (ideology removed)

Economy and public finances
- Eliminate most of the structural deficit within a Parliament; emergency Budget within 50 days; create an independent Office for Budget Responsibility; immediate £6bn savings; one‑year public sector pay freeze (excluding the lowest‑paid); reduce Whitehall and quango costs; cut ministers’ pay; reduce MPs by 10%.
- Modify 2011 National Insurance plans to reduce costs for employees under £35k and employers; lower and simplify business taxes (corporation tax to 25%, small companies to 20%) funded by relieving complex allowances; establish a five‑year corporate tax roadmap and an Office of Tax Simplification.
- Refocus R&D tax credits on hi‑tech SMEs; strengthen STEM, research stability and university‑business links; improve export support; promote saving (restore earnings link to state pension, auto‑enrolment) and end the effective annuity requirement at 75.
- Strengthen consumer finance protection (new agency, free national advice service, clearer credit card rules) and help manage unsecured debt.

Jobs, skills, welfare, immigration
- Single Work Programme for all unemployed; reassess incapacity claims; earlier, tailored, payment‑by‑results support; sanctions for refusal; community work placements; NI holiday for new firms’ first 10 hires; expand apprenticeships, work pairings and careers advice; free colleges from central control; 10,000 extra university places and HE funding reform.
- Set an annual limit on non‑EU economic migration; transitional controls for new EU members; English test for spouses; tighten student visas and require bonds for certain institutions.

- High‑speed rail linking major cities; no new runways at Heathrow, Stansted, Gatwick; rail franchise reform; consult on a Fair Fuel Stabiliser; superfast broadband via infrastructure sharing; replace RDAs with local enterprise partnerships; let councils keep part of business rate growth; open government procurement to SMEs.

Public services, transparency, banking
- Publish all central and local spending over low thresholds, senior salaries, and contracts; expand open data rights; support employee‑led mutuals to run services; reduce quangos; improve procurement governance.
- Bank levy; place prudential supervision with the central bank; curb risky activities, promote competition, and expand affordable SME credit.

Environment and energy
- Cut emissions 80% by 2050; 10% cut in central government emissions within 12 months; Green Investment Bank; carbon price floor; Green Deal (up to ~£6,500 per home); smart grid/meters; new nuclear (no subsidy); four CCS plants; offshore grid and marine energy; expand small‑scale and district heating.
- Protect habitats and marine zones; oppose whaling and ivory trade; criminalise illegal timber imports; plant up to 1m trees; reform fisheries and agriculture; tackle bTB (including targeted badger control); supermarket ombudsman; honest food labelling.

Families, health, education, social care
- Recognise marriage and civil partnerships in tax; end couple penalty in tax credits over time; two‑year council tax freeze; extend flexible working and shared parental leave; curb marketing to children; refocus Sure Start and add 4,200 health visitors.
- Real‑terms NHS funding growth; patient choice across qualified providers; GP‑led commissioning; publish outcomes; 24/7 urgent care and extended GP hours; protect local maternity/A&E where viable; Cancer Drugs Fund; new dentistry contract; personal budgets for long‑term conditions; support carers; voluntary insurance to protect homes from care costs; public health funding with a “health premium.”

- Tougher alcohol licensing; instant sanctions for ASB; prison sentences for knife crimes; extend magistrates’ powers; victim information; reduce police paperwork; directly elected local oversight of policing; monthly local crime data; Border Police Force; expand prison capacity; payment‑by‑results rehabilitation; abstinence‑based drug orders; temporary bans on new “legal highs.”

- Recall for MPs; cap big donations and tighten lobbying rules; citizen petitions to trigger debates; equalise constituencies; individual voter registration; backbench control of Commons time.
- Neighbourhood‑led planning; abolish regional targets; local referendums and vetoes on high council tax; community right to buy/run services; elected mayors in largest cities; general power of competence for councils.

Foreign, defence, aid
- National Security Council; Strategic Defence and Security Review; homeland defence command; sustain mission in Afghanistan; renew nuclear deterrent; cut MOD running costs ~25%; procurement reform; enhance support for service personnel and families.
- Active global engagement, alliances and human rights emphasis; EU “referendum lock” on future power transfers; no Euro adoption; seek return of specific powers.
- Legislate to spend 0.7% of national income on aid by 2013; full aid transparency; end aid to certain middle‑income countries; focus on basics and women/children/disabled; at least £500m/year on malaria; support trade, property rights and a Stabilisation & Reconstruction Force; climate‑smart, greener export support; promote a Pan‑African free trade area.

TEXT_G:
This manifesto proposes:

- Governance and democracy: Withdraw from the EU; introduce binding national and local referenda triggered by small voter thresholds; add proportional elements to elections; enable voter recall of MPs; abolish regional government bodies; create elected county-level Police, Health, and Education Boards; adjust devolution so Westminster MPs handle devolved matters part-time; establish English-only sittings at Westminster.

- Tax and economy: Raise the personal allowance to £11,500; introduce a 31% flat tax merging income tax and employee National Insurance; phase out employers’ National Insurance over five years; replace VAT with a Local Sales Tax shared with councils; share local business rates with councils; abolish Inheritance Tax when feasible; cut quangos and reduce the public sector to around its 1997 size; scrap EU-derived regulations; return bank oversight to the Bank of England, raise capital ratios, separate retail and investment banking, and reinstate lending controls.

- Jobs and industry: Major long-term investment in defence procurement, nuclear power, flood/coastal defences, transport infrastructure, and prison building; create Production Enterprise Centres to support SMEs; fund higher and further education via student/training vouchers and autonomous institutions; tighten takeover rules for strategic sectors; remove EU carbon-related business costs.

- Immigration and asylum: Five-year freeze on settlement; long-term cap (around 50,000 p.a.); time-limited work permits and visas with health insurance; tripled border staffing; record entries/exits; no amnesty for illegal residents; restore the Primary Purpose Rule; secure, expedited asylum processing with safe-country rule; repeal the Human Rights Act and withdraw from the ECHR; end government promotion of multiculturalism.

- Law and order: Elected police boards; “life means life”; double prison capacity; end early release; stronger self-defence rights; “three strikes” for repeat offenders; withdraw from the European Arrest Warrant; local referenda on major justice issues; boot camps for young offenders; abolish the Crown Prosecution Service.

- Defence: Increase spending by about 40%; expand the Army and Territorial Army; restore naval strength including three carriers; more helicopters and transport aircraft; maintain and replace the nuclear deterrent; prioritise NATO; streamline MOD bureaucracy; improve forces’ pay, conditions, and medical care.

- Health: Protect frontline NHS services; elected county health boards; reduce bureaucracy; franchise services on fixed budgets to a mix of providers; offer health credit vouchers to opt out; restore matrons and hospital-based nurse training; review community care; restore free eye tests and dental checks.

- Education: School vouchers usable at state, private, and faith schools; early literacy testing; retain/expand grammar and specialist schools with broader merit assessments; enhance classroom-based teacher training; end the 50% university target; replace loans with vouchers/grants; franchise schools; lighten the National Curriculum; abolish Ofsted; strengthen discipline; support special schools and home education.

- Pensions and welfare: A non-means-tested Citizen’s Pension of at least £130/week at 65; refocus tax relief on lower earners; reinstate the dividend tax credit; freeze unfunded public-sector pensions; simplify benefits into a Basic Cash Benefit (also used as student/training vouchers); allow earnings up to the tax threshold without losing BCB; merge and simplify child and nursery supports; restrict benefits to citizens/residents of five years; require workfare for some claimants.

- Foreign affairs and trade: Leave the EU and pursue a Swiss-style free-trade relationship; regain an independent WTO seat; seek a Commonwealth Free Trade Area; pursue agreements with blocs like NAFTA and ASEAN; promote democracy and self-determination.

- Energy and environment: Expand nuclear to up to 50% of electricity; support cleaner coal; shift large wind projects offshore and market-funded; repeal the Climate Change Act; exit EU carbon schemes and certain directives; commission an inquiry on climate science; refocus spending on practical environmental improvements; expand electrified transport; increase flood/coastal defences.

- Transport: Invest an extra £3bn p.a.; improve roads; share fuel duty windfalls with motorists; increase local control over parking/speed cameras; charge foreign lorries; block larger EU lorries; build three high-speed rail lines; reopen rail lines; shift freight to rail/canals; enhance port links; oppose extra Heathrow capacity; propose a Thames Estuary hub airport.

- Housing and planning: Curb housing demand by controlling immigration; bring empty homes into use; abolish regional planning frameworks and the Infrastructure Planning Commission; require binding local referenda for major developments; empower Green Belt conservators; scrap Section 106 and mandated social housing quotas; local listing; exempt listed-building refurbishment from the Local Sales Tax; scrap HIPs; allow council bonds for social housing; end empty-property business rates.

- Culture and public life: Create a register of key national brands; protect traditional weights/measures; bolster postal services; teach national historical contributions; restrict face coverings in specified settings; deport extremist preachers; reaffirm primacy of UK law over religious courts; establish Commonwealth Day and a new centre; adjust fiscal arrangements affecting England; mark St George’s Day as a holiday.

- Food, farming, and fishing: Regain independent agricultural and fisheries policy; maintain support during transition; promote British produce and ethical labelling; support GM research with clear labelling; review/replace EU rules; strengthen producer co-ops and a supermarket ombudsman; allow county hunting referenda; leave the Common Fisheries Policy; assert a 200-mile Exclusive Economic Zone; end quotas/discards; require all catches to be landed; create no-take zones; ban industrial fishing and certain trawling; expand fisheries protection.

- Other: Strengthen animal welfare; support pubs with designated smoking rooms; reduce burdens on small businesses.
